items: Initial blood alcohol concentration (BAC, %) = alcohol grams ÷ (body weight (g) × Widmark factor) × 100
Time to sober up (hours) = initial BAC ÷ elimination rate per hour (about 0.015%pt)

runs: The Widmark factor accounts for differences in body water distribution: 0.7 for men and 0.6 for women (so women reach a higher BAC at the same weight and drink amount).
. Actual alcohol metabolism varies a lot by individual — body composition, liver function, whether you ate, medications, and more. Don’t use this result to decide whether it’s safe to drive.
